newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-ELS JOINS THIRD TOUR.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELS JOINS THIRD TOUR.

text.p: World number four Ernie Els became the first professional golfer to belong simultaneously to three national circuits when he rejoined the European tour after a gap of two years on Friday.
Els, defending his South African crown at the Glendower Club, said in a statement that his move heralded a new trend in world golf.

"I began my international career in Europe and it's great to be playing more events there this year. With global television coverage of all the tours I think that multi-tour membership will become more common."
European Tour executive director Ken Schofield explained that a change to his tour's regulations had facilitated Els' decision.
"All three American majors will now count towards the number of events that European tour members must play, which is 11," Schofield said.
Els, who has already played two European co-sanctioned events in Australia this year, is now playing in his third European co-sanctioned event in Johannesburg.
With the three majors in America, Els needs to play in just five more events while keeping to his schedule of a minimum 15 events on the U.S. Tour, which he left Europe three years ago to join.

"He will be playing at Loch Lomond before the British Open," his manager Nick Frangos said. "He will also be playing in the BMW International Invitational (in Munich) and maybe the Irish Open if he can get a release from the US tour. Other than that we are not certain at this stage," said Frangos.
Els is also a member of the South African PGA tour but will only be playing in one event, the South African Open.
